_README: Human identification -> canonical name. THIS FILE SUPPLIES ONLY THE
IDENTIFICATION. The death year still comes from Wikidata via the normal
occupation-gated check, so nothing is promoted on recall alone. If a
canonical name does not resolve, the row stays held exactly as before.
Keys are either a bare name (applies everywhere) or 'identifier::name'
(applies to one item only, for fragments that are ambiguous in general).
Every entry records WHY, because a wrong identification here would ship a
protected work — this is the one place in the pipeline where a human error
is not caught by a later gate.

Joseph Concone.why: Schirmer editions anglicise Giuseppe Concone (Italian vocal-method composer) as 'Joseph'; the item is his Op. 24 melodic studies.

John Howard Paine.why: Source metadata typo ('Paine'); author of 'Home! Sweet Home!', which is the work in question.

Anna L. Waring.why: Welsh hymnwriter, author of 'In Heavenly Love Abiding' — the item's text.

F. Oakeley.why: Translator of 'Adeste Fideles' into 'O Come All Ye Faithful'; initial-only in the source.

Bishop H.U. Onderdonk.why: Episcopal bishop and hymnwriter; the source prefixes the title 'Bishop'.

Bud De Sylva.why: Buddy 'Bud' DeSylva, lyricist of 'Look for the Silver Lining'; source uses the nickname and splits the surname.

Jos. E. Howard.why: Abbreviated forename in the source; American songwriter.

Hart A. Wand.why: Composer of 'Dallas Blues'; source adds a middle initial.

ahsweetmysteryof00youn::Young.why: Item creator is the bare pair 'Young & Herbert' for 'Ah! Sweet Mystery of Life' — lyricist Rida Johnson Young. Item-scoped because 'Young' alone is meaningless generally.

ahsweetmysteryof00youn::Herbert.why: Same item; composer Victor Herbert. Item-scoped for the same reason.
